conventions.kjv: English Bible spelling of 1611/1769 (Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek names anglicised)
conventions.hebrew_inscr: DAHPN vocalised scholarly transcription; diacritics folded, aleph/ayin dropped, morpheme marks dropped
conventions.cuneiform_ctij: ORACC normalised Akkadian-style citation forms; diacritics folded (Judean and Babylonian names mixed; no language tag)
conventions.sumerian: ORACC ePSD2 citation forms; diacritics and index digits dropped
conventions.egyptian: Egyptological transliteration: consonants only, no vowels written
conventions.classical: Greek and Latin names in Latinised English print (Lempriere 1818, OCR)
conventions.census_1790: surnames and given names in the 1790 census returns (reprint of 1907-08, OCR), King James names removed
conventions.native_places: Algonquian and Iroquoian place names as spelled by English and Dutch writers (Beauchamp 1907, Trumbull 1881, OCR)
conventions.treaty_signers: native personal names as spelled by US treaty clerks (Kappler's text)
conventions.nahuatl: Nahuatl personal names in Spanish-based colonial spelling
conventions.maya: Classic Maya ruler names in modern epigraphers' spelling
conventions.hebrew_inscr_golub: Hebrew script mapped letter for letter to consonants (skeleton only)

skeleton_match_with_hebrew_inscriptions.note: added after the card was written (Tvedtnes, Gee and Roper 2000 arrived mid-run); a coarse consonant skeleton matches often by chance, which the other rows measure

wilcox_analogue.note: letters, not phonemes; an analogue of Wilcox et al., not a reproduction
